activities.title: Balance Shapes
activities.summary: Explore steady body shapes and choose how to make them easier to hold.

participation.adult_role: Demonstrate comfortable shapes, stay nearby and help the child adjust.

requirements: An adult checks a clear, level, firm area with space to stretch without contact.
The activity stays on the ground away from traffic and moving equipment.
setup: Begin with both feet on the ground in a comfortable position.
Explain that steady shapes can be small and both feet can stay down.
Agree that either person can change a shape, pause or stop whenever wanted.

5-7.challenge: Explore one steady shape at a time with both feet grounded.

steps.instruction: Keep both feet down and stretch your arms sideways.
steps.parent_prompt: Show a small comfortable stretch and check room around each person.

steps.instruction: Bring your arms close and make a smaller shape.
steps.parent_prompt: Keep both feet still; a smaller arm position is enough.

steps.instruction: Choose a shape that feels steady to you.
steps.parent_prompt: Invite the child to keep or change either demonstrated arm position.

5-7.ending: Return to a comfortable resting position and finish together.

8-10.challenge: Compare two arm positions and notice which feels steadier.

steps.instruction: Try a steady shape with your arms stretched sideways.
steps.parent_prompt: Keep both feet comfortably grounded; do not time the hold.

steps.instruction: Keep your feet still and try a different arm position.
steps.parent_prompt: Invite a comfortable change, then ask how it feels compared with the first.

steps.instruction: Adjust your arms to make your shape feel steadier.
steps.parent_prompt: Let the child decide; neither shape needs to be judged best.

8-10.ending: Relax the shape and describe one adjustment you noticed.

11-12.challenge: Design and adjust a controlled transition between two grounded shapes.

steps.instruction: Choose two comfortable shapes with both feet on the ground.
steps.parent_prompt: Help check space for both shapes and let the child choose arm positions.

steps.instruction: Move slowly between your shapes while keeping your feet grounded.
steps.parent_prompt: Let the child pause between shapes; there is no speed or holding target.

steps.instruction: Change one part to make the transition feel steadier.
steps.parent_prompt: Ask whether a smaller arm movement or a pause helps, then try the change.

11-12.ending: Return to rest and name the change that helped you.

simplify: Keep the arms close and use a smaller comfortable range of movement.
extend: Give each existing shape an imaginary name and repeat the same transition.

constraints: Keep both feet on the ground; do not add raised surfaces or one-leg challenges.
Do not add closed eyes, spinning, jumping, pushing or timed holding targets.
Stop or change any movement that feels uncomfortable or unsteady.
Story wording must retain the grounded positions and controlled transitions.

activities.title: Colour Hunt
activities.summary: Look for visible colours together and take turns choosing what to notice.

participation.adult_role: Help choose visible colours and accompany the child within the agreed area.

requirements: An adult checks a permitted observation area away from traffic and active sport.
Colours can be observed without touching objects or entering planting beds.
setup: Agree on a small area where the adult and child will stay together.
Look around together and choose a colour that is actually visible.
Explain that pointing or describing is enough; nothing needs to be collected.
Either person can pause or stop, and an unavailable colour can be changed.

5-7.challenge: Notice one visible colour and take a turn choosing another.

steps.instruction: Point to something with our chosen colour.
steps.parent_prompt: Choose a visible colour together and offer help locating it.

steps.instruction: Point to a different colour you can see.
steps.parent_prompt: Look from the same place or walk together within the agreed area.

steps.instruction: Choose a colour for me to find.
steps.parent_prompt: Let the child point out their choice if naming colours is difficult.

5-7.ending: Point to one favourite colour together, then finish the search.

8-10.challenge: Compare two visible colours and use a clue to guide a partner.

steps.instruction: Find two things with colours you can compare.
steps.parent_prompt: Stay together and use visible objects without handling them.

steps.instruction: Describe one colour difference between your two choices.
steps.parent_prompt: Accept the child's description; there is no correct shade to identify.

steps.instruction: Give me a colour clue for one thing you found.
steps.parent_prompt: Take a turn guessing from the checked area; let the child point if needed.

8-10.ending: Reveal the object from the clue and finish the search together.

11-12.challenge: Create a colour comparison rule and adjust it to what is visible.

steps.instruction: Choose a rule for comparing colours you can see.
steps.parent_prompt: Offer examples such as similar shades or a strong contrast; use the child's own descriptions.

steps.instruction: Find two visible examples and explain how they fit your rule.
steps.parent_prompt: Remain together; if examples are unavailable, invite a change to the rule.

steps.instruction: Teach me your rule and help me find another example.
steps.parent_prompt: Ask for a clue and search within the same area, adapting the rule if needed.

11-12.ending: Name one observation the rule helped you make, then finish.

simplify: Point together instead of naming or comparing colours.
Use a visible shape instead of colour if that is easier to distinguish.
extend: Swap who chooses the visible colour or comparison rule for another round.
Describe each observation as an imaginary clue without collecting anything.

constraints: Stay together within the checked area; a clue must never require searching beyond it.
Observe without picking, collecting, tasting or touching unknown objects.
Do not approach animals or strangers to inspect their colours.
Do not assume any particular plant, landmark or colour will be present.
Keep the observation tasks and ending when adding story wording.

activities.title: Follow the Leader
activities.summary: Take turns inventing and copying a short pattern of movements together.

participation.adult_role: Demonstrate, copy the child and help keep movements controlled.

requirements: An adult checks a clear, level area with room to move without contact.
The area is outside traffic, wheeled routes and play equipment landing areas.
setup: Stand facing each other with enough space to stretch arms without touching.
Agree to use gentle movements such as marching, arm circles or side steps.
Explain that either person can pause, change a movement or stop.

5-7.challenge: Copy one movement at a time and take a turn leading.

steps.instruction: Copy my slow marching steps.
steps.parent_prompt: March gently on the spot; let the child watch before joining.

steps.instruction: Copy my small arm circles.
steps.parent_prompt: Stop marching first, then demonstrate a comfortable arm circle.

steps.instruction: Choose a gentle movement for me to copy.
steps.parent_prompt: Offer the two demonstrated movements if the child wants help choosing.

5-7.ending: Choose one favourite movement and do it together, then stop.

8-10.challenge: Remember a two-movement pattern and notice a change in its order.

steps.instruction: Copy four marching steps, then two small arm circles.
steps.parent_prompt: Demonstrate the whole pattern slowly, then repeat it together.

steps.instruction: Put the arm circles first and try the pattern again.
steps.parent_prompt: Let the child organise the two movements; offer a demonstration if wanted.

steps.instruction: Choose two gentle movements and teach me your pattern.
steps.parent_prompt: Follow the child's pattern without scoring memory or counting errors.

8-10.ending: Perform the child's two-movement pattern together once, then stop.

11-12.challenge: Design, teach and adapt a three-movement pattern for a partner.

steps.instruction: Choose three gentle movements and arrange them into a pattern.
steps.parent_prompt: Agree which movements fit the space; let the child decide their order.

steps.instruction: Teach me your pattern one movement at a time.
steps.parent_prompt: Copy each movement, then ask the child to lead the combined pattern.

steps.instruction: Change one part so the pattern is easier to copy.
steps.parent_prompt: Invite a change to order, repetition or movement size, then try it together.

11-12.ending: Perform the adapted pattern together once and name the change, then stop.

simplify: Use one comfortable movement at a time and copy it together.
Use small arm movements while staying in place if preferred.
extend: Swap leaders for another round using movements already agreed with the adult.
Give the same movements an imaginary character without adding new actions.

constraints: Keep movements gentle, within the checked area and in the adult's sight.
Do not add climbing, backward travel, chasing, contact or speed competitions.
Do not require equipment, landmarks or surfaces absent from the requirements.
Keep the listed tasks and each age variant's ending when adding story wording.

activities.title: Imaginary Delivery
activities.summary: Pretend to carry a make-believe parcel and decide how to deliver it together.

participation.adult_role: Join the pretend delivery and agree any movements within the checked space.

requirements: An adult checks a small, clear, level area with room for a few forward steps together.
The delivery begins and ends within that area, away from traffic and active play.
setup: Agree on a nearby imaginary delivery spot inside the checked area.
Explain that there is no real parcel to find, pick up or carry.
Use comfortable arm movements and slow forward steps; staying in place is also allowed.
Either person can change the pretend idea, pause or stop.

5-7.challenge: Imagine one parcel and act out delivering it with an adult.

steps.instruction: Pretend you have a soft, light parcel in your hands.
steps.parent_prompt: Offer a simple imaginary parcel such as a cushion; nothing is actually held.

steps.instruction: Carry your pretend parcel beside me with slow steps.
steps.parent_prompt: Walk together towards the agreed spot, or mime the delivery in place.

steps.instruction: Show me how you give me the pretend parcel.
steps.parent_prompt: Mime receiving it without requiring touching or carrying any real object.

5-7.ending: Set the imaginary parcel down in the story and relax your arms.

8-10.challenge: Choose an imaginary parcel's shape and adapt how you carry it.

steps.instruction: Choose whether your pretend parcel is wide or narrow.
steps.parent_prompt: Keep the imagined parcel light and use only comfortable arm positions.

steps.instruction: Show how you carry that shape to our delivery spot.
steps.parent_prompt: Move together slowly within the checked area or mime the steps in place.

steps.instruction: Pretend its shape changes and adjust your delivery movements.
steps.parent_prompt: Stay at the delivery spot and use smaller arm movements if needed.

8-10.ending: Hand over the pretend parcel and describe how its shape changed your actions.

11-12.challenge: Plan a pretend delivery and adapt it when the imaginary parcel changes.

steps.instruction: Invent a light parcel and explain your delivery plan.
steps.parent_prompt: Agree the nearby destination first; the plan uses the same checked space.

steps.instruction: Act out carrying your parcel towards our agreed delivery spot.
steps.parent_prompt: Walk beside the child with slow forward steps, or perform the delivery in place.

steps.instruction: Imagine its shape changes and decide how to adjust your plan.
steps.parent_prompt: Pause the walking and let the child adapt the arm movements without expanding the area.

steps.instruction: Show your adjusted delivery and explain what you changed.
steps.parent_prompt: Play the receiver and let the child finish using the agreed movements.

11-12.ending: Complete the handover in the story, then return your arms to rest.

simplify: Mime the whole delivery in place with small arm movements.
Let the adult suggest the parcel while the child chooses how to carry it.
extend: Swap sender and receiver roles using the same area and movement limits.

constraints: All parcels are imaginary; do not collect, lift or deliver real objects.
Remain together within the checked area; do not approach strangers as recipients.
Do not add obstacles, roads, water, climbing, running or jumping to the story.
Keep the parcel light in the story and every movement comfortable.
Future story wording must retain the same delivery area and permitted actions.

activities.title: Notice the Change
activities.summary: Take turns changing a small part of a pose and noticing what is different.

participation.adult_role: Show small pose changes, keep the child in sight and offer clues when wanted.

requirements: An adult checks a clear, level area where the pair can stand without contact.
Both people can observe each other without blocking routes or active play.
setup: Face each other with enough room for small arm movements.
Agree to stay in place and change only comfortable hand or arm positions.
When a change is hidden, the child looks to one side with eyes open and stays still.
Either person can request a clue, pass a turn or finish the activity.

5-7.challenge: Notice one visible change and then choose a change yourself.

steps.instruction: Watch my hands and point to what changes.
steps.parent_prompt: Slowly change one hand from open to closed while the child watches.

steps.instruction: Tell me or show me which hand changed.
steps.parent_prompt: Show the original and new positions again if the child wants help.

steps.instruction: Change one hand position for me to notice.
steps.parent_prompt: Describe what you see; the child does not need to copy your example.

5-7.ending: Reveal the last change and return both hands to rest.

8-10.challenge: Remember a pose and identify one change after looking away.

steps.instruction: Look at my arm positions, then look to one side.
steps.parent_prompt: Stay nearby with the child in sight; change one small arm position.

steps.instruction: Look back and describe the change you notice.
steps.parent_prompt: Offer a clue or show both poses again; guessing is optional.

steps.instruction: Choose one pose change for me to spot.
steps.parent_prompt: Look at the child's feet while they change one arm, keeping them in sight.

8-10.ending: Explain the final change to each other and return to rest.

11-12.challenge: Compare two pose changes and choose a useful clue for an observer.

steps.instruction: Study my hand and arm positions, then look to one side.
steps.parent_prompt: Make two small comfortable changes while keeping the child in sight.

steps.instruction: Look back and explain the two differences you notice.
steps.parent_prompt: Offer a comparison with the original pose; there is no score for recall.

steps.instruction: Choose a pose change and a clue to help me notice it.
steps.parent_prompt: Keep the child in sight while looking at their feet, then look up and use the clue.

11-12.ending: Reveal the change and explain how the clue helped, then relax.

simplify: Make one slow change while the observer watches the whole time.
Point or demonstrate instead of describing the change in words.
extend: Swap who invents the change and who gives a clue for another round.

constraints: Stay in place with eyes open; do not add hiding, blindfolds or searching elsewhere.
The adult must keep the child in sight throughout each turn.
Change only comfortable hand or arm positions; do not require contact or props.
Story wording must preserve the observation and comparison tasks.

activities.title: Pass and Move
activities.summary: Roll a soft ball to a partner, then change position together for the next pass.

participation.adult_role: Roll the ball gently, agree each position and retrieve loose balls only when appropriate.

required: A soft ball suitable for rolling between the child and adult.

requirements: An adult checks a level, clear area where a ball can roll without entering traffic or active play.
There is room for the pair to change position without contacting other people.
The family brings the ball; the location dataset does not establish equipment availability.
setup: Face each other a short, comfortable rolling distance apart.
Agree to roll along the ground and stop the ball before changing position.
Agree that the child will wait if the ball leaves the checked area.
Either person can pause, move closer or end the game at any point.

5-7.challenge: Stop and return a gentle roll, then move to an agreed position.

steps.instruction: Stop the ball I roll towards you.
steps.parent_prompt: Roll gently from nearby and let the child choose a comfortable way to stop it.

steps.instruction: Roll the ball back towards me.
steps.parent_prompt: Stay close and make the receiving position easy to see.

steps.instruction: Hold the ball while we each take one sideways step.
steps.parent_prompt: Check room first, move together, then stop and exchange another gentle roll.

5-7.ending: Stop the ball after one final exchange and finish together.

8-10.challenge: Compare two rolling distances and choose one that helps the pair cooperate.

steps.instruction: Exchange two gentle rolls from our starting positions.
steps.parent_prompt: Stop the ball between turns and count exchanges together without scoring.

steps.instruction: Hold the ball while we choose a second rolling distance.
steps.parent_prompt: Agree a small change within the checked area, stop moving, then exchange two rolls.

steps.instruction: Choose which distance made the ball easier to control.
steps.parent_prompt: Move to the chosen positions while holding the ball, then try another exchange.

8-10.ending: Stop the ball and describe which distance worked for you both.

11-12.challenge: Plan and improve a short pattern of positions for cooperative rolling.

steps.instruction: Choose two nearby positions for our rolling pattern.
steps.parent_prompt: Agree positions within the checked area; no markers or field lines are needed.

steps.instruction: Guide us through one exchange at each position.
steps.parent_prompt: Hold the ball during every position change and roll only when both people are still.

steps.instruction: Change one position to make the next exchange easier to control.
steps.parent_prompt: Discuss the change, move while holding the ball and repeat the adjusted pattern.

11-12.ending: Stop the ball after the adjusted pattern and name the change together.

simplify: Stay in one position and shorten the distance between partners.
Stop each roll with help from the adult before taking another turn.
extend: Swap who chooses the positions while keeping the same checked area and rolling rules.
Treat the same gentle rolls as delivering an imaginary parcel.

constraints: Roll on the ground; do not add throwing, kicking, striking or speed targets.
Stop and hold the ball before changing position; do not chase a moving ball.
If the ball leaves the checked area, the child waits with the activity paused.
Do not assume nets, hoops, painted lines, markers or supplied equipment.
Keep the rolling and position-change rules when adding story wording.
